correctness.rationale: For all connected graphs on at most three vertices, complete graph-shape analysis gives pairwise ordering fixed on edges and triangles and at most one center-leaf crossing on a three-path, since the leading eigenvalue decreases strictly in mutation intensity. For the positive-rate four-path witness (1,8,2,3), exact determinant arithmetic yields a common-root resultant u^4(2u^3-13u^2+22u-10). Three exact rational root intervals exhaust the cubic. The first candidate gives a non-Perron eigenvalue below 1; the other two give eigenvalues above 4, hence necessarily principal since the second eigenvalue is at most 3. Simplicity of the cubic and eigenvalues makes the two frequency ties strict crossings. The small-mutation ratio 6/7 and high-mutation coefficient -1/8 verify the orientation. The delivered standalone script reproduces the algebraic identities and branch checks; optional numerical examples are supplementary.

value.rationale: The precise object is an experimentally motivated normalized mutation-selection equilibrium on the smallest nontrivial graph motif beyond three genotypes. The theorem proves the sharp network-size cutoff for reentrant pairwise abundance rankings, not just a hand-picked numerical sign flip. The two compared genotypes are both one mutation away from a dominant fitter genotype but have different additional mutation routes; their lower-fitness member becomes more abundant only over an explicit intermediate mutation window. This clarifies when single-rate genotype frequency comparisons cannot extrapolate across mutation intensities and supplies a reproducible four-genotype benchmark. It neither asserts a large practical effect nor generalizes to other mutation mechanisms.
